title: Ergodic Decomposition: Mathlib Has the Extreme-Point Structure
description: The parent (furstenberg-correspondence-oq-02) is a feasibility survey of formalizing ergodic decomposition that is unsure whether the key structural fact — ergodic measures are exactly the extreme points of the invariant probability measures — is in Mathlib. This entry resolves that: the characterization IS in Mathlib (Ergodic.iff_mem_extremePoints), together with ergodic rigidity (Ergodic.eq_of_absolutelyContinuous) and a.e.-constancy of invariant functions (PreErgodic.ae_eq_const_of_ae_eq_comp). We package these as the concrete building blocks of ergodic decomposition, answering the OQ: Mathlib's disintegration plus this extreme-point theory supplies the structure; the remaining gap is the Choquet integral representation. 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext:
The ergodic decomposition theorem says that any invariant measure of a measure-preserving system can be written uniquely as an integral of ergodic measures: μ = ∫ μ_x dμ(x), where each μ_x is ergodic. Structurally this is a Choquet-type result: the invariant probability measures form a convex set (in fact a simplex), the ergodic measures are exactly its extreme points, and the decomposition expresses a general invariant measure as a barycentre (integral) over those extreme points. Realising the integral concretely uses disintegration of measures with respect to the invariant σ-algebra.

The parent gallery entry surveyed the feasibility of formalizing this in Lean and was uncertain whether the central piece — the identification of ergodic measures with the extreme points — was already in Mathlib, noting it 'might already be partially there'. In fact Mathlib's `Mathlib.Dynamics.Ergodic.Extreme` proves the full equivalence `Ergodic.iff_mem_extremePoints`, along with the rigidity `Ergodic.eq_of_absolutelyContinuous` and (in `Ergodic.Function`) the a.e.-constancy of invariant functions. This entry confirms and packages these, recording the honest answer to the OQ: the extreme-point structure and disintegration are present; the outstanding work for the full theorem is the Choquet integral representation tying a general invariant measure to its ergodic components.
overview.problemStatement: Determine whether Mathlib provides the structural prerequisites for the ergodic decomposition theorem. Confirm and package: (1) ergodic measures are exactly the extreme points of the invariant probability measures; (2) ergodic measures are rigid (an absolutely continuous invariant probability measure equals the ergodic one); (3) invariant measurable functions are a.e. constant under an ergodic measure.
overview.proofStrategy: Each result is a direct invocation of Mathlib's verified ergodic theory, restated in gallery form: ergodic_iff_extremePoint = Ergodic.iff_mem_extremePoints; ergodic_eq_of_absolutelyContinuous = Ergodic.eq_of_absolutelyContinuous; ergodic_invariant_ae_const = (Ergodic.toPreErgodic).ae_eq_const_of_ae_eq_comp. The bundled ergodic_decomposition_prerequisites assembles all three for an ergodic probability measure.
keyInsights: Ergodic measures ARE the extreme points of the invariant probability simplex — the Choquet picture underlying ergodic decomposition — and Mathlib already proves this equivalence (Ergodic.iff_mem_extremePoints).

Ergodic rigidity (an absolutely continuous invariant measure equals the ergodic one) is the statement that distinct ergodic components are mutually singular, so the decomposition is a partition into disjoint pieces.
A.e.-constancy of invariant functions makes the decomposition map (point ↦ its ergodic component) well defined: the invariant σ-algebra is a.e. trivial on each component.

The honest answer to the parent's OQ: disintegration plus the extreme-point theory supplies the structure; what is still missing is the Choquet integral representation (writing a general invariant measure as ∫ over its ergodic components).
Confirming a result already exists in Mathlib is itself a useful contribution to a feasibility survey: it converts 'might be there' into a verified, citable fact.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 81 lines and 4 theorems confirming and packaging the structural prerequisites for ergodic decomposition that Mathlib already provides: ergodic ⟺ extreme point of the invariant probability measures, ergodic rigidity, and a.e.-constancy of invariant functions.
conclusion.implications: This answers the parent survey's OQ: Mathlib's disintegration together with its ergodic extreme-point theory supplies the structure for ergodic decomposition — the characterization the survey was unsure existed is in fact in Mathlib (Ergodic.iff_mem_extremePoints). The honest remaining gap for the full theorem is the Choquet integral representation expressing a general invariant measure as an integral over its ergodic (extreme) components. Recording these as verified, citable facts converts the survey's uncertainty into concrete building blocks.
